\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مخالفة} (mukhālafa)}{مخالفة (mukhālafa)}]{\ar{مخالفة} (mukhālafa) — an offence; a traffic ticket}

\label{lesson:AR-C352-mukhalafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to forge, then the Arabic for to conceal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مخالفة}}
\textbf{\ar{مخالفة}} — \emph{mukhālafa} — \textquotedblleft{}an offence; a traffic ticket\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حصل} \ar{أبي} \ar{على} \ar{مخالفة} \ar{أمس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaṣala abī ʿalā mukhālafa ams.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father got a traffic ticket yesterday.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مخالفة}} (\emph{mukhālafa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-l-f} (Lane), the root of the taught \emph{khalfa}, behind. \emph{Mukhālafa} is the verbal noun of Form III, \textquotedblleft{}going against\textquotedblright{} a rule.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukhālafa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukhālafa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaṣala abī ʿalā mukhālafa ams.} — My father got a traffic ticket yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to forge, then the Arabic for to conceal, then say \emph{mukhālafa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مخالفة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An offence; a traffic ticket\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{غرامة} (gharāma)}{غرامة (gharāma)}]{\ar{غرامة} (gharāma) — a fine, a penalty fee}

\label{lesson:AR-C352-gharama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to conceal, then the Arabic for an offence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{غرامة}}
\textbf{\ar{غرامة}} — \emph{gharāma} — \textquotedblleft{}a fine, a penalty fee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{الغرامة} \ar{خمسين} \ar{دينارا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat al-gharāma khamsīn dīnāran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fine was fifty dinars.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{غرامة}} (\emph{gharāma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{gh-r-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to pay a debt or a fine\textquotedblright{}; \emph{gharām}, passion, is the same root, a love that will not let go.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gharāma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat al-gharāma khamsīn dīnāran.} — The fine was fifty dinars.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to conceal, then the Arabic for an offence, then say \emph{gharāma} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شجار} (shijār)}{شجار (shijār)}]{\ar{شجار} (shijār) — a brawl, a quarrel}

\label{lesson:AR-C352-shijar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an offence, then the Arabic for a fine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شجار}}
\textbf{\ar{شجار}} — \emph{shijār} — \textquotedblleft{}a brawl, a quarrel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وقع} \ar{شجار} \ar{بين} \ar{رجلين} \ar{في} \ar{المقهى}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waqaʿa shijār bayna rajulayn fī al-maqhā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A fight broke out between two men in the café.
\end{quote}

The taught \ar{تشاجر}, to quarrel, is the same root.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شجار}} (\emph{shijār}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-j-r} (Lane), the root of \emph{shajara}, a tree, where branches tangle; \emph{tashājara} is \textquotedblleft{}to get tangled with one another\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shijār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shijār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waqaʿa shijār bayna rajulayn fī al-maqhā.} — A fight broke out between two men in the café.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an offence, then the Arabic for a fine, then say \emph{shijār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{شجار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A brawl, a quarrel\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ضجة} (ḍajja)}{ضجة (ḍajja)}]{\ar{ضجة} (ḍajja) — a commotion, an uproar}

\label{lesson:AR-C352-dajja}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a fine, then the Arabic for a brawl.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ضجة}}
\textbf{\ar{ضجة}} — \emph{ḍajja} — \textquotedblleft{}a commotion, an uproar\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أحدث} \ar{الخبر} \ar{ضجة} \ar{كبيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aḥdatha al-khabar ḍajja kabīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The news caused a big stir.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ضجة}} (\emph{ḍajja}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-j-j} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to cry out, to clamour\textquotedblright{}; \emph{ḍajīj} is noise.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حشد} (ḥashd)}{حشد (ḥashd)}]{\ar{حشد} (ḥashd) — a crowd, a gathering}

\label{lesson:AR-C352-hashd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a brawl, then the Arabic for a commotion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حشد}}
\textbf{\ar{حشد}} — \emph{ḥashd} — \textquotedblleft{}a crowd, a gathering\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انتظر} \ar{حشد} \ar{كبير} \ar{أمام} \ar{الملعب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intaẓara ḥashd kabīr amāma al-malʿab.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A big crowd waited in front of the stadium.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{حشود}, \emph{ḥushūd}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حشد}} (\emph{ḥashd}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-sh-d} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to gather people together\textquotedblright{}; \emph{ḥashd} is the gathering.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
